title: Enterprise Sales Kit: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical enterprise sales kit for Redwood Inference: a single pack combining positioning & messaging, short competitive briefs, pitch deck highlights, pricing guidance, 2 vetted case studies, and a security FAQ for prospects. Use this during discovery and technical validation calls.

Owners & escalation
- Primary author: Aisha Patel (go-to-market)
- Sales enablement owner: Michael Chen
- Technical reviewer: Laura Gomez (solutions engineering)
- Enterprise escalation: Jorge Martinez (sales leadership)

How to use this kit
1. For early discovery: open with the Positioning blurb and customer problem statements.
2. For technical validation: share the Competitive brief + Security FAQ and schedule a short demo with Solutions Engineering.
3. For procurement: use the Pricing Guidance section and attach the Pricing appendix (PDF) to the proposal.

Positioning & Messaging (elevator + 3 core themes)
- Elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — delivering predictable latency, better unit economics, and enterprise-grade controls so product teams can ship LLM features without owning the serving stack.

- Core themes for messaging (use based on audience):
  - Developer velocity: Rapid self-serve onboarding, SDKs, and pre-built prompt templates minimize time-to-first-call and integration effort.
  - Production economics & reliability: Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations, and routing policies reduce cost while meeting latency SLOs.
  - Flexible deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private/VPC or on-prem options for regulated workloads.

Key customer problems we solve
- Unpredictable inference cost at scale
- Slower-than-expected latencies from generic hosting solutions
- Operational burden of model rollouts and regressions
- Gaps in security/compliance for regulated environments

Value metrics (talk track)
- Typical latency improvement vs baseline managed endpoints: 30–60% (model & workload dependent)
- Typical per-token cost reduction after enablement: 20–45% driven by batching + caching + quantization profiles
- Mean time to onboard a model into production (developer + infra): 1–4 weeks (self-serve to Dedicated contract)

Competitive brief (short summaries + callouts)
- Cloud AI Provider A (managed endpoints)
  - Strengths: Simple API, large model catalog, global cloud infra.
  - Weaknesses vs Redwood: Less predictable unit economics at high QPS, fewer production-grade routing/fallback features, limited private deployment options.
  - Win criteria: Customers who need lower latency variability and predictable unit economics.

- Self-hosted runtime (open-source + infra)
  - Strengths: Full control, potentially lower VM-only cost.
  - Weaknesses vs Redwood: High ops cost, slower time-to-production, lacks unified rollout/observability that ties model quality regressions to prompts.
  - Win criteria: Customers who have large ops teams and strict regulatory needs but are willing to build everything in-house.

- Inference vendor B (closed ecosystem, accelerator ties)
  - Strengths: Highly optimized for specific HW, good latency for narrow workloads.
  - Weaknesses vs Redwood: Tight hardware lock-in, limited model interchangeability, less flexible deployment modes for enterprise multi-region needs.
  - Win criteria: Customers optimizing a single, stable model on a single hardware fabric.

Competitive talking points matrix (one-slide summary)
| Dimension | Redwood Inference | Cloud Provider A | Self-hosted | Vendor B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment Modes | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Hosted | Private (self) | Hosted/Dedicated (HW lock) |
| Cost Predictability | High (reserved + tooling) | Medium | Low (ops cost) | Medium |
| Latency SLOs & Fallbacks | Strong (routing + compatible variants) | Medium | Variable | Strong (hardware-specific) |
| Observability | Token-level, per-route, regressions | Basic | Custom-built | Limited |
| Time-to-production | Fast (SDKs, templates) | Fast | Slow | Medium |

Pitch deck highlights (one-slide per bullet — use in demo deck)
1. Problem statement: rising inference cost, latency variability, and operational burden. (Include customer quote from Case Study A)
2. Redwood solution: unified runtime + orchestration + deployment modes. (Diagram: request routing -> runtime -> caching/batching -> metrics)
3. Architecture & key differentiators: kernel selection, continuous batching, KV cache, smart routing policies.
4. Performance & cost outcomes: sample benchmark (internal): 40% cost reduction, 35% latency median improvement for conversational workloads.
5. Security & compliance: private deployment, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SOC2-ready artifacts.
6. Customer stories: Case Study A (Fintech) and Case Study B (Healthcare).
7. Pricing & commercial motion: Self-serve hosted -> Dedicated commits -> Private licensing model.

Pricing guidance (sales playbook)
- Pricing model overview:
  - Hosted: consumption-based (per-token + per-embedding). Typical deal coverage for SMB/Startups.
  - Dedicated: reserved capacity (monthly/annual commit) priced by GPU-equivalent units + support tier. Predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at commit > $50k/mo.
  - Private: platform license + deployment fee + optional managed services. Enterprise contracts and custom SLAs.

- Example pricing bands (use as conversational guidance only — attach legal appendix for firm quotes):
| Plan | Target profile | Commercial model | Typical ARR range |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Self-serve Hosted | Startups / small dev teams | Pay-as-you-go | $0 – $50k |
| Dedicated Starter | Growing product teams | 3–12 month commit | $50k – $250k |
| Dedicated Scale | Large product orgs | Annual reserved capacity | $250k – $2M+ |
| Private | Regulated enterprises | License + deployment + support | $500k – $5M+ |

- Discounting guidelines:
  - Competitive chase discounting should be compensated by CSM enablement/co-terming.
  - Standard approval threshold: up to 20% by AEs; >20% requires Rev Ops + Sales Leadership.
  - For multi-year/strategic deals, involve Legal/Finance for custom billing terms.

Contracting & SLA talking points
- Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime target for GPU pools (region-specific), latency SLOs based on route/profile.
- Security add-ons: extended audit log retention, dedicated network peering, on-prem bundle.

Case studies (customer-ready summaries)
- Case Study A — Fintech: Real-time underwriting assistant
  - Customer problem: High latency and token cost on baseline managed endpoints causing poor user experience for live underwriting.
  - Scope: Conversational underwriting flow, 2M tokens/day, peak QPS 120.
  - Solution: Dedicated deployment with prefix caching on user session keys, intelligent batching and quantization profile for the model family.
  - Outcome: 38% reduction in median latency, 33% reduction in per-token cost, rollback-safe canary rollout used for model update.
  - Contactable quote: "Redwood cut our inference cost and gave us predictable SLA behavior — our underwriting throughput doubled." — VP Product (redacted)

- Case Study B — Healthcare (PHI-sensitive POC): Clinical documentation assistant (on-prem/private)
  - Customer problem: Strict data residency and PHI controls prevented use of public managed endpoints.
  - Scope: On-prem Private deployment, HSM/KMS integration, audit logging and SOC2 artifacts provided.
  - Solution: Private control plane with local inference, formal runbooks for upgrade/rollback, and custom retention policy.
  - Outcome: Successful pilot with HIPAA-required controls, 95% clinician satisfaction in pilot, path to Dedicated for non-PHI flows.

Security FAQ for prospects (short answers)
- Q: Can Redwood run entirely inside our VPC / on-prem?
  - A: Yes. We offer Private (VPC) deployments and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. See related: confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention.
- Q: How do you handle encryption & key management?
  - A: Customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed encryption with optional CMEK.
- Q: Do you provide audit logs and retention policies for compliance?
  - A: Yes. Audit logging is configurable; extended retention plans are available as an add-on. See confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging.
- Q: What certifications / evidence do you provide?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II readiness artifacts and can share redacted reports under NDA. For Private deployments, customers manage their own audit evidence for the local environment.
- Q: How is data used for model training / telemetry?
  - A: By default, customer data is not used to train Redwood models. We provide explicit settings and contracts; details available in the security FAQ and contract addendum.
- Q: How do you isolate multi-tenant Dedicated customers?
  - A: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and strict network and storage separation; we also offer role-based access controls (RBAC) and per-tenant audit trails.

Demo checklist for Solutions Engineering
1. Confirm deployment mode the prospect needs (hosted / dedicated / private).
2. Prep the demo model & dataset (ensure representative latency and sequence lengths).
3. Run live benchmark: show median & p95 latency, throughput, token cost delta vs baseline.
4. Walk through rollout: canary -> metrics -> automatic fallback.
5. Review security controls and audit logging.
